description: We are a two-person team combining data analysis, coding, and design to tackle real-world space challenges. Passionate about leveraging NASA datasets, rapid prototyping, and creative problem-solving. Note: Our team is currently complete and not looking for additional members for this hackathon, but we’re excited to connect with other teams and share ideas!
summary:
It is an edge-deployed 3D planetary radar observatory developed for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge. The Great Rann of Kutch—Earth’s largest seasonal salt desert—suffers from two catastrophic blind spots under conventional optical satellites: total cloud-cover blindness during the four-month monsoon deluge, and severe sun-glare saturation from crystalline halite flats in winter.
It solves this challenge by harnessing calibrated 24cm L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data from the NASA-ISRO NISAR mission (Level-2 GCOV, 1.25 GHz, Track 063 / Frame 076). Because 24cm microwaves penetrate cloud decks and dry salt crusts up to 1.5 meters, SAANS renders the invisible: tracking the rapid 96-hour transformation of 7,505 km² of bone-dry playa into a 20,500 km² inland sea, mapping the natural 1.5m brine moat protecting 500,000 nesting Greater Flamingos, quantifying Banni grassland biomass, and revealing the active 1819 Allah Bund seismic fault.
Combining interactive 3D WebGL strata, multi-temporal radar sliders, and an 8,960-bead phosphor matrix, SAANS unites spaceborne microwave physics with 600 years of indigenous pastoral climate resilience.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO OR HOW DOES IT WORK?

SAANS is an interactive, browser-based 3D Earth Observation observatory that transforms multi-gigabyte Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) granules from the joint NASA-ISRO NISAR mission into an intuitive, sequential spatial exploration. Users explore the Great Rann of Kutch across three dynamic hydrological and ecological regimes:

1. The Arid Winter Regime: Features an interactive 3D exploded strata stack peeling back surface co-polarized backscatter (HH: -14.2 dB), vegetative cross-polarized volume scatter (HV: -21.0 dB), and subterranean dielectric permittivity (up to 1.5m depth), exposing the 1819 Allah Bund earthquake fault scarp and hidden alluvial aquifers.

2. The Monsoon Inundation Regime: An interactive flood dynamics slider and 10-pass multi-temporal radar sequence tracking 20,513.7 km² of peak storm inundation, specular water reflection nulls (< -22 dB), and the natural brine moat safeguarding 500,000 nesting Greater Flamingo chicks on Khadir Island.

3. The Savanna & Indigenous Resilience Regime: An interactive 4-tier isometric canopy penetration cuboid (2.5m tree crowns down to 0.2m root soil) and an 8,960-bead illuminated phosphor matrix showcasing pastoral Maldhari communities and circular mud Bhungas, which withstood the 2001 Bhuj magnitude 7.7 earthquake with 0% structural shear collapse.

WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

- Overcomes Optical Blindness: Optical sensors (Landsat, Sentinel-2) are 100% blinded by monsoon storm clouds and blinded by winter halite albedo glare. NISAR's 24cm L-band microwave radar penetrates both effortlessly.

- Zero-Bandwidth Edge Architecture: The entire client bundle is under 1.1 MB of JavaScript with lossless WebP radar textures under 8 MB total payload, running locally at a locked 60 FPS without requiring cloud GPUs or continuous high-bandwidth internet.

- Universal Educational Accessibility: Provides dual exploration lenses—"For Everyone" (interactive physical analogies) and "Physics" (Bragg scattering, dielectric constants, and radar equations)—making aerospace data accessible to students, researchers, rangers, and policymakers alike.

WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT OF THE PROJECT?

- Ecological Conservation: Enables wildlife rangers to track seasonal water levels around vulnerable Greater Flamingo breeding mounds and assess grazing pressures across 15,510 km² of the Indian Wild Ass (Khur) sanctuary.

- Grassland Commons Management: Equips indigenous Maldhari pastoralists and local authorities with real-time pasture biomass data (up to 28.5 Mg/ha) across 2,618 km² of unfenced Banni savanna, helping manage rotational grazing and monitor invasive Prosopis juliflora spread.

- Disaster & Structural Resilience: Demonstrates how spaceborne radar monitoring of active tectonic faults (Allah Bund) combined with vernacular architectural wisdom (circular hoop-tension mud Bhungas) provides vital lessons for modern disaster-resilient housing.

WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE DID YOU USE?

- Frontend Architecture: React 18, Vite 5.4, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, GSAP.

- 3D Rendering & Simulation: Three.js (WebGL 2.0), Canvas 2D particle simulation, responsive procedural coordinate projection.

- Radar Data Processing: Python, GDAL, NumPy, and H5py for ingesting NASA/ISRO Level-2 Geocoded Covariance (L2-GCOV) HDF5 granules, converting radiometric power to calibrated sigma-naught decibels, directional inpainting of SweepSAR antenna gaps, and lossless WebP matrix export.

- Deployment: Vercel Global Edge CDN, Git version control.

HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

Rather than displaying static satellite maps or complex scientific dashboards, SAANS fuses physical museum-grade spatial design with cutting-edge radar remote sensing. Instead of standard flat images, we created an 8,960-bead phosphor dot matrix with real-time magnetic cursor repulsion, serving as an interactive metaphor for discrete spaceborne radar resolution cells. Furthermore, SAANS pairs quantitative aerospace metrics with 600 years of indigenous oral climate knowledge and authentic field recordings.

WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

- Radiometric Scientific Integrity: Calibrated all decibel thresholds against official NASA JPL NISAR calibration models and peer-reviewed geological benchmarks.

- Remote Rural Access: Designed for low-power mobile laptops and tablets without requiring specialized GPU hardware.

- Cultural Representation: Accurately reflected the living pastoral heritage of Maldhari communities and Harappan archaeological water engineering at Dholavira without synthetic caricature or generic AI imagery.
